Nothing in Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust, simply known in Japan as Vampire Hunter D (バンパイアハンターD, Banpaia Hantā Dī), is a 2000 dark fantasy vampire adventure anime film written for the screen and directed by Yoshiaki Kawajiri. The film began production in 1997 and was completed with the intention of being shown in American theaters.

The psychology underneath Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust is simpler and older than the story on top. The New York Daily News referred to the film as "Beautiful, witty and provocative" and that it should "appeal to fans and non-fans alike".
